Hayy Arts | Global Positioning System

Opening May 20, 2026, ‘Global Positioning System’ is an upcoming exhibition curated by Indranjan Banerjee and Lucas Morin. Global Positioning System is an exhibition dedicated to mapping and navigation systems. It tells stories of fast cars and slow trains, street barriers and trembling grounds, warping highways and broken bridges.

Hayy Arts | Red Wind, Coral Worlds

Opening May 20, 2026, ‘Red Wind, Coral Worlds’ is an upcoming exhibition curated by recipients of the Art Jameel Curatorial Open Call, Huda Tayob and Miriam Hillawi Abraham. Red Wind, Coral Worlds sites the Red Sea within an expanded and interconnected oceanic terrain. The exhibition traces the entangled worlds that converge across its waters, attending to the material and affective remnants left in the wake of centuries of movement and migration shaped by trade, pilgrimage, and displacement.

Hayy Learning | Recess: An After-School Programme for Teens

Recess is back — and applications are open! An alternative afterschool arts programme at Hayy Jameel for ambitious teens aged 14–17. Over 12 weekly sessions, participants dive into contemporary art through studio practice, research, field trips to local galleries and artist studios and mentorship from working creatives. Every student hand-binds their own portfolio throughout the programme, and the whole cohort comes together at the end for a real, student-led showcase.

Hayy Cinema | “Kef Hayyak?” 3rd Edition Screenings and Awards Ceremony

Join us for the screenings of the third edition of “Kef Hayyak?” cohort’s films! “Kef Hayyak?” is a unique documentary filmmaking challenge that invites aspiring filmmakers to capture the essence of their neighborhoods in Jeddah through their own lens—using only their phones. Building on the success of its first two editions, the programme launched an open call for its third edition in December 2025, selecting 13 projects for development based on the quality and originality of their creative proposals.

Jameel Library | Summer Reading Challenge

Jameel Library invites you to build a relationship with the library through curiosity, discovery, and spending time exploring its resources. This challenge celebrates the moments you spend here cultivating new interests and passions rather than the number of books you finish. Throughout July and August, participants will receive prizes based on the number of hours they spend at Jameel Library, turning every visit into a small seed planted among the shelves, and nurtured with every new visit.

Hayy Explorers | As Told by The Land: Traces & Memory

As Told by the Land is a three-month long thematic programme at Hayy Explorers for children aged 6–15 years old. Through educational programmes and artist interventions, it responds to the current Hayy Arts exhibitions by exploring themes of storytelling, movement, and shifting worlds. Across the three months, children are invited to follow paths, collect traces, and construct new worlds from their immediate surroundings and everyday life.

Hayy Makers | Woodworking Course (Level 2) with Ahmad Sofi

An intermediate woodworking course focused on advancing technical skills through machine work, carving, joinery, design planning, and finishing techniques. Participants will gain the confidence to execute more complex projects with precision and craftsmanship. * Completion of the Foundations of Woodworking Course (Level 1) or equivalent prior woodworking experience is required. Learning Outcomes: Learn workshop safety protocols and proper use of personal protective equipment. Use Jigs and modify machine cuts.

Hayy Makers | Introduction to Pottery Course with Pharah Al-Ghalib

This intensive three-day course with artist and designer Pharah Al-Ghalib offers a comprehensive introduction to wheel-thrown pottery, guiding participants through the full spectrum of the ceramic process. Day 1 Clay & Wheel Fundamentals: Focuses on understanding clay—its qualities, preparation, and potential. Participants will learn wedging techniques before moving to the wheel to practice centering, opening, and pulling walls, creating several forms to be set aside to dry to a leather-hard stage.
